about.title: About Freight World
about.metaDescription: What Freight World is, where its data comes from and under which licences.
about.lead: Freight World generates truck jobs that could leave today from cities that exist in American Truck Simulator, and later Euro Truck Simulator 2. It is not a game and not a real freight exchange: nobody drives anything here.

rules.real: Cities, companies, depots, cargo and trailers come only from the game, as documented on Truck Simulator Wiki. Nothing is invented.
rules.unknown: What is not known for certain is stored as empty or marked as an estimate, never guessed.
rules.ids: Internal game IDs are kept where the wiki gives them, so live game data can be linked later.
rules.images: No logos, screenshots or other images from the games. City photos come from Wikimedia Commons with author and licence.

about.sourcesIntro: The sources Freight World uses. Game data covers the starting map of American Truck Simulator: California, Nevada and Arizona.
about.sourcesCaption: Data sources, their use and their licences.
about.attributionIntro: This text appears in the footer of every page:
about.datasetTitle: Licence of the Freight World dataset
about.datasetText: The game data files Freight World publishes are derived from Truck Simulator Wiki and are shared under the same licence, CC BY-SA 4.0.
about.gamesText: American Truck Simulator and Euro Truck Simulator 2 are games by SCS Software. Freight World is an independent fan project and is not affiliated with SCS Software.

mission.metaDescription: Full sheet of one American Truck Simulator job: depots, cargo, trailer, truck, route, weather and DLCs.
mission.badId: This job link is not valid.
mission.gone: This job no longer exists in the game data (a depot, cargo or trailer changed). Generate a new one.
mission.noGameId: No game ID on the wiki
mission.companyTrailer: Company trailer, not sold at the dealer
mission.noTrailerData: No dealer data for this trailer type
mission.night: Arrival at night: plan a rest stop or a delivery window.
mission.severe: Bad weather: {what} in {city}. Drive carefully; the drive time above does not include delays.
mission.truckRule: Freight World rule (simulated, not from the game): at least 400 hp up to 25,000 lb, 450 hp up to 45,000 lb, 500 hp above, 550 hp for heavy cargo; brands with a dealer in the start city first; electric trucks left out (no range data).
mission.provenance: Depots, cargo, trailers and trucks: Truck Simulator Wiki (CC BY-SA 4.0). Distance and drive time: estimates from real roads (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL) at 55 mph. Weather: MET Norway (CC BY 4.0). Pay is not shown: the game’s pay inputs are not public.
mission.deliverBy: Deliver by {time} in {city} (if you accept it now)
mission.realTimeLine: Planned trip {game} in game ≈ {real} min of real driving (1 game hour = 3 real minutes outside cities).
mission.urgencyRule: Urgency and time to deliver: a Freight World rule (simulated, not the game’s formula). The time allowed is the planned trip plus a margin: 50% standard, 25% important, 10% urgent (at least 1 hour).
mission.planRule: US Hours of Service (FMCSA): at most 11 hours of driving, a 30-minute break after 8 hours of driving, 10 hours off before driving again. Stricter than the game, which asks for sleep every 14 in-game hours. Loading and unloading time not included.
mission.chainIntro: So you do not drive back empty: real jobs leaving {city}. Jobs that fit the trailer you already have come first, then jobs heading back.
mission.chainAll: All jobs from {city} in the planner
